chunk_findings.detail: `unrelated` treats every failed `git merge-base` as “no history in common” and tells the caller to `git branch -m` the task branch aside and cherry-pick. `merge-base` also exits non-zero for a bad base name or a missing object (exit 128), not only for exit 1 (“no merge base”). Given an existing `ddflow/T1` that does share history with `main`, and `base="no-such"` (or a corrupt/partial repo where the merge-base object is missing), `have_branch` is true, this still raises `GitError` with the rename/cherry-pick remedy, and following that text renames a branch that was not unrelated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_basecheck.py:23

chunk_findings.detail: `test_claim_command_refuses_an_unrelated_branch_with_the_remedy` is named and documented as locking the remedy, but it only asserts `code != 0` and the substring `"no history in common"`. A claim path that prints that phrase and drops ``git branch -m`` / cherry-pick still passes, so the CLI contract the test claims to pin is not actually checked.
